transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-23
Start: 09:30 PDT
Duration: 1h2m
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Emily Zhou (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Aisha Khan (Nimbus Procurement), Marcus Lee (Nimbus Security), Priya Desai (Nimbus FinOps), Daniel Ortiz (Nimbus Legal), Rhea Iyer (Nimbus Platform)

Summary:
Quick procurement and legal handoff to align on MSA/DPA exceptions, SLA tiers, egress billing model, and KMS/keying approach for a pilot + production guardrails. FinOps will drive sizing & cost acceptance; Security wants KMS + SOC2/FedRAMP path clarified.

Topics covered:
- Pricing and egress fee structure (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- KMS integration and key management options (bring-your-own-key, Redwood-managed)
- MSA/DPA exception path and timeline for redlines
- SLA tiers and rollback/fallback policies for inference routing
- Pilot metrics: QPS, token/month, P95 latency targets

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I know we have the procurement cross functional group here so we'll run through pricing, egress, and then handoff to legal and security for DPA/MSA redlines. If anyone wants to add to the agenda, jump in.

[00:00:22] Aisha (Nimbus - Procurement): Thanks Samir. Quick ask — we'll need the egress model split by region and by deployment mode. FinOps wants to see worst case so they can size the commit.

[00:00:35] Priya (FinOps): Yeah, exactly. We have two things: month zero pilot and then projected steady state. We need both token burn and egress bytes for cost. Are egress fees per-request or per-GB?

[00:00:50] Emily (Redwood SE): Good question. Egress is modelled two ways right now — for hosted API there's a per-token compute charge plus a network egress per-GB if they leave our cloud region. For Dedicated and Private we can show a different breakdown; Private often sits behind your VPC so network egress depends on your cloud egress rules. We'll share a spreadsheet.

[00:01:12] Marcus (Security): Quick clarification — when you say Private behind VPC, are we sending requests over a private peering or is there a public egress hop? Security needs high level on traffic path and any TLS termination points.

[00:01:30] Emily (SE): For Redwood Private with VPC peering, traffic stays over the peering link; TLS terminates at the customer's ingress if you're running the on‑prem package. For Redwood Dedicated (hosted but reserved) TLS terminates in our infra. We'll note the difference in the doc. Apologies if I mumbled earlier — the auto transcript may show K-V cache as K-V cake, ugh.

[00:01:58] Samir: No worries. On KMS — two options: 1) Redwood-managed keys with envelope encryption (fastest onboarding), or 2) BYOK with customer KMS (we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations). Marcus, is BYOK a hard requirement?

[00:02:20] Marcus: We prefer BYOK for tokenization keys and any persisted cache. For pilot we can accept Redwood-managed keys if we have key rotation SLAs and proof of controls, but for production we want customer keys in our KMS and HSM-style assurance. Also need to confirm that KV cache is never written to third-party logs.

[00:02:40] Emily: Understood. We have a KMS integration note that shows the rotation process — I'll share it after the call. There's also a compliance pack (SOC2 + ISO summary) and a FedRAMP pathway doc we've started for regulated customers.

[00:03:05] Daniel (Legal): On the MSA/DPA side, a couple of asks: first, Nimbus needs the DPA to include clear subprocessor lists and 30 day notification for data incidents, second, we have some egress/egress fee language that conflicts with our procurement standard. We'll send redlines, but timeline wise we need the initial MSA back within ten business days for internal review.

[00:03:26] Samir: Ten business days is tight but doable; our legal team will aim for a first-pass. Jordan from CSM will be the ops contact for pilot. Jordan?

[00:03:35] Jordan (CSM): Yup, I’ll own the pilot ops schedule and share the runbook. I'll coordinate with Rhea for technical oncalls and Emily for the KMS handovers.

[00:03:48] Aisha: For pricing — if we go hosted with a commit, what discounts do you typically provide? Also curious about overage mechanics and rate cards for P95 latency SLOs.

[00:04:05] Samir: For reserved commits (Dedicated), discounts scale with monthly commit. The spreadsheet I'll send shows tiers: no commit (on-demand), small commit (discount ~15%), mid (25%), enterprise (40%+ depending on term and usage). Overage is billed at the committed rate plus a markup for bursts — we'll include an example calculation. Latency SLO tiers are separate — SLO for P95 is part of the SLA and higher tiers include financial credits.

[00:04:33] Priya: We need an explicit egress cap and a model showing worst-case egress fees if all traffic hits US-East then replicates to users in EU. Also any double-billing edge cases — e.g., if we have a VPC peering but also fall back to public endpoints during failover.

[00:04:52] Emily: Good point. Failover routing can cause temporary egress changes; we have fallback rules that route to a compatible model variant in a different region which can create cross-region egress. We'll annotate typical failover scenarios and the expected egress multiplier.

[00:05:12] Rhea (Platform Eng): For engineering, we need the token-cost per API call for our internal forecasting. Also what metrics do you expose for tracing — per-request token count, model version, KV cache hit/miss?

[00:05:27] Emily: We expose token counts, model_id, model_version, latency buckets, cache_hit boolean, and route_id. Trace logs are available in Console; we can stream to your SIEM via webhook or S3 drop. We'll share a sample export.

[00:05:45] Marcus: Is there an audit log for key access and rotation events? Our auditors will want those logs retained for 12 months at minimum.

[00:05:56] Emily: Yes — key access events are logged and can be included in the audit trail. Retention windows are configurable with the enterprise plan; we'll include retention options in the compliance pack.

[00:06:12] Daniel: On liability and indemnity we have standard ask to limit IP indemnity carveouts for model hallucinations. We need to align on acceptable language; I'll flag the exact clauses in the redline.

[00:06:26] Samir: Understood. We do common carveouts for outputs that are generated by models — we can discuss mitigations like prompt filters and eval gating. Emily, do we have a recommended eval / monitoring pattern for production?

[00:06:38] Emily: Yes — Redwood Optimize supports regression alerts tied to prompt sets. For production we recommend a small eval harness and an automatic rollback policy to previous model version when quality drops. We'll link to the eval playbook.

[00:06:55] Priya: Who will own ongoing cost reporting? We need token-level cost broken down by route and team for internal chargebacks.

[00:07:05] Jordan: We can enable route-level cost tags and a billing export that maps tokens to route_id and team tags. Jordan will set up a weekly report during pilot.

[00:07:17] Aisha: Ok — timeline check. We want pilot kickoff second week of August. Deliverables needed before pilot: MSA/DPA first-pass, egress/pricing spreadsheet, KMS integration notes, runbook and ops oncall. Can Redwood meet that?

[00:07:33] Samir: Yes, if we get Rhea's ingestion profile by Fri (2026-07-24) we'll finalize the pricing model and send the packet by Mon (2026-07-26). Legal will try to return the MSA first-pass within ten business days as Daniel requested.

[00:07:45] Daniel: We'll get Rhea and procurement to respond quickly. Also want to schedule a legal redline walkthrough after you send first-pass. Prefer a 30 minute slot.

[00:07:56] Samir: Sounds good. Jordan, can you coordinate the redline walkthrough?

[00:08:01] Jordan: Yes — I'll propose times in the calendar.

[00:08:08] Marcus: One more security nuance — we require periodic penetration testing and notice of infra changes that affect data paths. Is that covered?

[00:08:18] Emily: We can include pentest attestations and a change notice SLA in enterprise plans. For pilot we can provide the latest pentest report and schedule a quarterly attestation.

[00:08:33] Aisha: Thanks. A couple of small items — procurement prefers to see an escalation path and an executive sponsor from Redwood for contract issues.

[00:08:44] Samir: I'll be the named sponsor for procurement escalations and Jordan will be ops sponsor. We'll put both on the MSA cover sheet.

[00:08:52] Priya: Great. If we can get the pricing by Monday we can run a FinOps signoff by Wednesday.

[00:08:59] Samir: Ok wrapping up — recap of next steps and owners, and we'll follow up with artifacts: pricing spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/pricing/nimbus-egress), KMS integration note (link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/kms-integration), and MSA first-pass target.

[00:09:20] Daniel: Quick note — please mark the MSA as "DRAFT - Nimbus redline expected" in the subject so our legal tracker can find it.

[00:09:28] Jordan: Will do.

[00:09:32] Samir: Awesome. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email and calendar invites.

[00:09:38] Aisha: Thanks all.

[00:09:40] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (K-V cache -> K-V cake in raw transcript), filler words preserved (uh, mm), parentheticals included. Shared artifacts referenced as short links above.
